questions.s: 15% of Rs 2,400 is
questions.e: 15% of 2,400 = 0.15 × 2,400 = Rs 360 (10% is 240 and 5% is 120). Rs 240 is only 10%, and Rs 3,600 comes from multiplying by 1.5 instead of 0.15.

questions.s: Rs 4,500 is divided between Ali and Bilal in the ratio 4 : 5. Bilal's share is
questions.e: The ratio has 4 + 5 = 9 parts, so one part is 4,500 ÷ 9 = Rs 500 and Bilal gets 5 × 500 = Rs 2,500. Rs 2,000 is Ali's share, and Rs 2,250 is simply half the money.

questions.s: The price of a school bag is increased by 20% and the new price is then reduced by 20%. Compared with the original price, the final price shows
questions.e: Final price = 1.20 × 0.80 = 0.96 of the original, which is a 4% decrease. The two 20% changes do not cancel because the reduction is taken on the larger, increased price.

questions.s: The average of five numbers is 18. When a sixth number is included, the average becomes 20. The sixth number is
questions.e: Sum of five numbers = 5 × 18 = 90; sum of six numbers = 6 × 20 = 120. The sixth number is 120 − 90 = 30. Answering 20 just repeats the new average, which ignores the change in the total.

questions.s: A shopkeeper buys a shirt for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 1,000. His profit percentage is
questions.e: Profit = 1,000 − 800 = Rs 200, and profit % = 200/800 × 100 = 25%. Dividing the profit by the selling price gives 20%, but profit percentage is always taken on the cost price.

questions.s: Sana sold an old mobile phone for Rs 1,530 at a loss of 10%. The cost price of the phone was
questions.e: At a 10% loss, SP = 90% of CP, so CP = 1,530 ÷ 0.9 = Rs 1,700. Adding 10% of the selling price (1,530 + 153 = 1,683) is wrong because the 10% is a percentage of the cost price.

questions.s: The simple interest on Rs 12,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years is
questions.e: SI = P × R × T / 100 = 12,000 × 8 × 3 / 100 = Rs 2,880. Rs 960 is the interest for one year only.

questions.s: Fatima deposits Rs 10,000 at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. The interest she earns in 2 years is
questions.e: Amount = 10,000 × 1.1² = 10,000 × 1.21 = Rs 12,100, so the interest is 12,100 − 10,000 = Rs 2,100. Rs 12,100 is the amount, not the interest, and Rs 2,000 is the simple interest.

questions.s: A car covers 180 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. Its average speed is
questions.e: 2 hours 30 minutes = 2.5 h, so speed = 180 ÷ 2.5 = 72 km/h. Taking the time as 2 h gives 90 km/h, which ignores the extra half hour.

questions.s: Hamza drives from Islamabad to a nearby town at 60 km/h and returns along the same road at 40 km/h. His average speed for the whole trip is
questions.e: For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) = 2 × 60 × 40 / 100 = 48 km/h. The simple average 50 km/h is wrong because more time is spent at the slower speed.

questions.s: A train 150 m long runs at 54 km/h. The time it takes to pass an electric pole is
questions.e: 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. To pass a pole the train covers its own length, so time = 150 ÷ 15 = 10 s. Dividing 150 by 54 without converting units gives about 2.8, which mixes km/h with metres.

questions.s: A train 200 m long, running at 72 km/h, crosses a platform completely in 25 seconds. The length of the platform is
questions.e: 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so in 25 s the train covers 20 × 25 = 500 m. This distance is train plus platform, so the platform is 500 − 200 = 300 m. Answering 500 m forgets to subtract the train's own length.

questions.s: Ali can paint a room in 12 days and Hamza can paint it in 6 days. Working together, they can paint it in
questions.e: Per day they finish 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/12 + 2/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the room, so together they need 4 days. Averaging 12 and 6 to get 9 days is wrong: working together must be faster than the faster worker alone.

questions.s: Pipe A can fill a water tank in 6 hours and pipe B can empty the full tank in 9 hours. If both pipes are opened together on the empty tank, it will be full in
questions.e: Net filling per hour = 1/6 − 1/9 = 3/18 − 2/18 = 1/18, so the tank fills in 18 hours. 3.6 hours comes from adding the rates, as if B were also filling the tank.

questions.s: A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.e: Milk = 30 L and water = 10 L. For milk : water = 3 : 2 the water must be 20 L, so 20 − 10 = 10 L must be added. 20 litres is the final amount of water, not the amount added.

questions.s: The HCF of 36 and 60 is
questions.e: 36 = 2² × 3² and 60 = 2² × 3 × 5; the HCF takes the lowest common powers, 2² × 3 = 12. 180 is the LCM, not the HCF.

questions.s: The LCM of 8, 12 and 18 is
questions.e: 8 = 2³, 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3²; the LCM takes the highest powers, 2³ × 3² = 72. 36 is not a multiple of 8 and 24 is not a multiple of 18.

questions.s: Three school bells ring at intervals of 6, 8 and 12 minutes. If they ring together at 9:00 a.m., they will next ring together at
questions.e: They ring together again after LCM(6, 8, 12) = 24 minutes, at 9:24 a.m. Adding the intervals (6 + 8 + 12 = 26) gives 9:26, which is not a common multiple.

questions.s: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.e: 97 has no prime factor up to √97 ≈ 9.8 (it is not divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 7), so it is prime. 51 = 3 × 17, 87 = 3 × 29 and 91 = 7 × 13 only look prime.

questions.s: The four-digit number 52A6 is divisible by 9. The digit A is
questions.e: A number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is a multiple of 9. 5 + 2 + A + 6 = 13 + A, and the only digit making it a multiple of 9 is A = 5 (sum 18). A = 4 gives 17, which is not divisible by 9.

questions.s: The value of 3/4 of 2/5 of 600 is
questions.e: 2/5 of 600 = 240, and 3/4 of 240 = 180. Stopping after the first step gives 240, which takes only 2/5 of the number.

questions.s: 0.25 × 0.4 equals
questions.e: 25 × 4 = 100, and the factors have 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places, so the product is 0.100 = 0.1. Counting only two decimal places would wrongly give 1.

questions.s: Which of the following fractions is the greatest?
questions.e: As decimals: 5/8 = 0.625, 3/5 = 0.6, 7/12 ≈ 0.583 and 2/3 ≈ 0.667, so 2/3 is the greatest. 7/12 has the largest numerator and denominator but is actually the smallest.

questions.s: Ayesha's salary is 25% more than Zainab's. By what percentage is Zainab's salary less than Ayesha's?
questions.e: If Zainab earns 100, Ayesha earns 125. Zainab's salary is less by 25 out of 125, which is 25/125 × 100 = 20%. 25% is wrong because the comparison is now made with Ayesha's larger salary.

questions.s: A pair of shoes is marked at Rs 2,500 and sold at a discount of 12%. The sale price is
questions.e: Discount = 12% of 2,500 = Rs 300, so the sale price is 2,500 − 300 = Rs 2,200. Subtracting Rs 120 treats 12% of 1,000 as the discount and gives the wrong Rs 2,380.

questions.s: A shopkeeper in Lahore marks his goods 40% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. His profit percentage is
questions.e: If CP = 100, the marked price is 140 and the selling price is 90% of 140 = 126, so the profit is 26%. Subtracting the percentages (40 − 10 = 30%) ignores that the discount is taken on the higher marked price.

questions.s: If a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5, then a : c is
questions.e: Make b equal in both ratios: a : b = 8 : 12 and b : c = 12 : 15, so a : c = 8 : 15. Simply joining the outer terms of the given ratios (2 : 5) ignores that b has different values.

questions.s: Rs 6,250 grows to Rs 7,840 in 2 years at compound interest, compounded annually. The rate of interest per annum is
questions.e: 7,840/6,250 = 1.2544 = (1.12)², so the yearly growth factor is 1.12 and the rate is 12%. 12.72% is the simple-interest rate for the same gain (1,590 over 2 years), which ignores compounding.

questions.s: In how many years will Rs 5,000 earn Rs 1,500 simple interest at 6% per annum?
The average mark of 20 students was found to be 45. Later it was found that one student's mark of 64 had been read as 46. The correct average is
questions.e: Wrong total = 20 × 45 = 900; the correct total is 900 + (64 − 46) = 918, so the correct average is 918 ÷ 20 = 45.9. 44.1 comes from subtracting the error of 18 instead of adding it.

questions.s: Walking at 4/5 of his usual speed, Usman reaches school 10 minutes late. His usual time to reach school is
questions.e: At 4/5 of the speed the time becomes 5/4 of the usual time t, so the delay is t/4 = 10 minutes and t = 40 minutes. 50 minutes is the time taken at the slower speed.

questions.s: Two trains 120 m and 180 m long run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 40 km/h and 50 km/h. The time they take to cross each other completely is
questions.e: In opposite directions the relative speed is 40 + 50 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, and the distance is 120 + 180 = 300 m, so the time is 300 ÷ 25 = 12 s. 108 s uses the difference of speeds (10 km/h), which applies only to trains moving in the same direction.

questions.s: 12 workers can build a boundary wall in 15 days. How many workers are needed to build it in 10 days, working at the same rate?
questions.e: The job needs 12 × 15 = 180 worker-days, so in 10 days 180 ÷ 10 = 18 workers are needed. 8 workers comes from treating workers and days as directly proportional; fewer days need more workers.

questions.s: In what ratio must rice costing Rs 240 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs 300 per kg so that the mixture costs Rs 260 per kg?
questions.e: By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (300 − 260) : (260 − 240) = 40 : 20 = 2 : 1. Check: (2 × 240 + 300)/3 = 780/3 = 260. The ratio 1 : 2 reverses the two parts and would give Rs 280 per kg.

questions.s: What percentage of 80 is 20?
questions.e: 20/80 × 100 = 25%. Taking 20 as the percentage itself gives 20%, which would be 16, not 20.

questions.s: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 78. The largest of the three numbers is
questions.e: Let the numbers be n − 2, n and n + 2; then 3n = 78, so n = 26 and the largest is 28. 26 is the middle number, not the largest.

questions.s: The population of a town is 50,000 and it grows by 4% every year. Its population after 2 years will be
questions.e: Population = 50,000 × 1.04² = 50,000 × 1.0816 = 54,080. 54,000 adds 4% of 50,000 twice, which forgets that the second year's growth is on 52,000.

questions.s: Successive discounts of 20% and 10% on a marked price are equivalent to a single discount of
questions.e: The customer pays 0.80 × 0.90 = 0.72 of the marked price, so the single equivalent discount is 28%. Adding the discounts to get 30% ignores that the 10% is taken on the already reduced price.

questions.s: The smallest number which leaves a remainder of 4 when divided by each of 6, 9 and 15 is
questions.e: LCM(6, 9, 15) = 90, and adding the remainder gives 90 + 4 = 94. 86 subtracts the remainder instead, and 184 = 180 + 4 also works but is not the smallest.

questions.s: 6 notebooks cost Rs 540. At the same rate, 10 notebooks cost
questions.e: One notebook costs 540 ÷ 6 = Rs 90, so 10 notebooks cost Rs 900. Rs 1,080 is the price of 12 notebooks.

questions.s: If 3x − 7 = 11, then x equals
questions.e: Add 7 to both sides: 3x = 18, so x = 6. Subtracting 7 instead of adding gives 3x = 4 and the wrong value 4/3.

questions.s: If 2(x + 3) = 5x − 9, then x equals
questions.e: Expand: 2x + 6 = 5x − 9, so 15 = 3x and x = 5. Check: 2(8) = 16 = 25 − 9. The value −5 comes from a sign slip, writing −15 = 3x when collecting the constants.

questions.s: The roots of the equation x² − 5x + 6 = 0 are
questions.e: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3), so x = 2 or x = 3. The pair −2 and −3 has the right product but sum −5, which would need +5x in the equation.

questions.s: For the equation 2x² − 8x + 6 = 0, the sum and the product of the roots are
questions.e: For ax² + bx + c = 0, sum = −b/a = 8/2 = 4 and product = c/a = 6/2 = 3 (the roots are 1 and 3). Sum 8 and product 6 forget to divide by the leading coefficient 2.

questions.s: If x + y = 10 and x − y = 4, then y equals
questions.e: Adding the equations gives 2x = 14, so x = 7, and then y = 10 − 7 = 3. The value 7 is x, not y.

questions.s: In a Peshawar stationery shop, 3 pens and 2 registers cost Rs 340, while 1 pen and 1 register cost Rs 130. The price of one pen is
questions.e: Let pen = p and register = r. From p + r = 130, r = 130 − p; then 3p + 2(130 − p) = 340 gives p + 260 = 340, so p = Rs 80 and r = Rs 50. Rs 50 is the price of a register.

questions.s: The solution of the inequality 2x − 5 < 7 is
questions.e: Add 5: 2x < 12, then divide by the positive number 2: x < 6. The sign is not reversed because we did not multiply or divide by a negative number.

questions.s: The solution of the inequality −3x + 4 ≥ 13 is
questions.e: Subtract 4: −3x ≥ 9. Dividing by −3 reverses the sign, giving x ≤ −3. Forgetting to reverse the sign gives x ≥ −3, which fails for x = 0 (4 ≥ 13 is false).

questions.s: The value of 2⁵ × 2³ ÷ 2⁴ is
questions.e: Add and subtract the powers: 2⁵⁺³⁻⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Multiplying the indices (5 × 3) instead of adding them is a common slip.

questions.s: The value of 27^(2/3) is
questions.e: 27^(2/3) = (∛27)² = 3² = 9. The value 18 comes from multiplying 27 by 2/3 instead of using it as a power.

questions.s: If 3^(x + 1) = 81, then x equals
questions.e: 81 = 3⁴, so x + 1 = 4 and x = 3. Answering 4 forgets that the exponent is x + 1, not x.

questions.s: The value of log₂ 32 is
questions.e: log₂ 32 asks which power of 2 gives 32; since 2⁵ = 32 the value is 5. 16 is 32 ÷ 2, which confuses a logarithm with division.

questions.s: Using logarithms to base 10, log 2 + log 5 equals
questions.e: log a + log b = log (ab), so log 2 + log 5 = log 10 = 1. log 7 wrongly adds the numbers inside the logs, and 10 is the number whose log is taken, not the log itself.

questions.s: If log₃(x − 1) + log₃(x + 1) = 1, then x equals
questions.e: Combine: log₃[(x − 1)(x + 1)] = 1, so x² − 1 = 3 and x = ±2. x = −2 is rejected because log₃(−3) is undefined, leaving x = 2.

questions.s: The 20th term of the arithmetic sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, … is
questions.e: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d = 7 + 19 × 4 = 83. Using n instead of n − 1 gives 7 + 20 × 4 = 87.

questions.s: The sum of the first 20 terms of the arithmetic series 3 + 7 + 11 + … is
questions.e: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d] = 10 × (6 + 76) = 10 × 82 = 820. Forgetting the factor 1/2 gives 1,640.

questions.s: In a geometric sequence the 3rd term is 12 and the 6th term is 96. The first term is
questions.e: ar⁵ ÷ ar² = r³ = 96/12 = 8, so r = 2 and a = 12/r² = 12/4 = 3. The value 2 is the common ratio, not the first term.

questions.s: Bilal saves Rs 500 in the first month and increases his saving by Rs 100 every month. His total savings after 12 months are
questions.e: The savings form an AP with a = 500 and d = 100; the 12th month's saving is 500 + 11 × 100 = 1,600. Total = 12/2 × (500 + 1,600) = 6 × 2,100 = Rs 12,600. Rs 6,000 ignores the monthly increase.

questions.s: If f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1, then f(−2) equals
questions.e: f(−2) = 2(4) − 3(−2) + 1 = 8 + 6 + 1 = 15. Getting 3 treats −3 × −2 as −6, a sign error.

questions.s: If f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x², then f(g(2)) equals
questions.e: First g(2) = 4, then f(4) = 3 × 4 − 2 = 10. The value 16 is g(f(2)) = g(4), which applies the functions in the wrong order.

questions.s: If f(x) = (x + 5)/3, then the inverse function f⁻¹(x) is
questions.e: Write y = (x + 5)/3, so x = 3y − 5; swapping the letters gives f⁻¹(x) = 3x − 5. Check: f(3x − 5) = 3x/3 = x. The reciprocal 3/(x + 5) is not an inverse function.

questions.s: The slope of the straight line through the points (1, 2) and (4, 11) is
questions.e: Slope = (11 − 2)/(4 − 1) = 9/3 = 3. Taking the run over the rise gives 1/3, the reciprocal of the slope.

questions.s: The line 2x + 3y = 12 cuts the y-axis at y equal to
questions.e: On the y-axis x = 0, so 3y = 12 and y = 4. The value 6 is where the line cuts the x-axis (y = 0 gives 2x = 12), and −2/3 is the slope.

questions.s: Which of the following points lies on the line y = 2x − 3?
questions.e: Substitute x = 2: y = 4 − 3 = 1, so (2, 1) lies on the line. For (0, 3) the line gives y = −3, so that point uses the wrong sign of the intercept.

questions.s: The equation x² + kx + 16 = 0 has two equal roots and k is positive. The value of k is
questions.e: Equal roots need b² − 4ac = 0: k² − 64 = 0, so k = 8 (taking the positive value); the equation is then (x + 4)² = 0. Answering 4 uses k² = 16 and forgets the factor 4ac.

questions.s: The sum of a number greater than 1 and its reciprocal is 10/3. The number is
questions.e: x + 1/x = 10/3 gives 3x² − 10x + 3 = 0, i.e. (3x − 1)(x − 3) = 0, so x = 3 or 1/3. Since the number is greater than 1, it is 3; 1/3 is its reciprocal.

questions.s: Mr Ahmed is 4 times as old as his son. In 5 years he will be 3 times as old as his son. The son's present age is
questions.e: Let the son be s: 4s + 5 = 3(s + 5) gives s = 10. Check: now 40 and 10; in 5 years 45 and 15, and 45 = 3 × 15. 40 years is the father's age.

questions.s: A rectangular plot has a perimeter of 70 m and an area of 300 m². Its length (the longer side) is
questions.e: l + w = 35 and lw = 300, so l and w are roots of t² − 35t + 300 = 0, i.e. (t − 20)(t − 15) = 0. The length is 20 m and the width 15 m; 15 m is the shorter side.

questions.s: The vertex (turning point) of the graph of y = x² − 6x + 5 is
questions.e: x = −b/2a = 6/2 = 3 and y = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4, so the vertex is (3, −4); equivalently y = (x − 3)² − 4. (−3, −4) uses x = b/2a and has the wrong sign.

questions.s: For x ≠ 3, (x² − 9)/(x − 3) simplifies to
questions.e: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), and cancelling x − 3 leaves x + 3. Cancelling x² with x and 9 with 3 term by term is not allowed.

questions.s: A cinema in Karachi sold 200 tickets for a show. Adult tickets cost Rs 500 and child tickets Rs 300, and the total takings were Rs 84,000. The number of adult tickets sold was
questions.e: a + c = 200 and 500a + 300c = 84,000. Substituting c = 200 − a: 200a + 60,000 = 84,000, so a = 120 and c = 80. 80 is the number of child tickets.

questions.s: The solutions of |2x − 3| = 7 are
questions.e: 2x − 3 = 7 gives x = 5, and 2x − 3 = −7 gives x = −2. Taking only the positive case misses the second solution.

questions.s: If 4ˣ − 3 · 2ˣ − 4 = 0, then x equals
questions.e: Put t = 2ˣ, so 4ˣ = t²: t² − 3t − 4 = 0 gives (t − 4)(t + 1) = 0. Since 2ˣ > 0, t = 4 and x = 2. The answer 4 is the value of 2ˣ, not x.

questions.s: When x = 3, the value of x² − 2x + 4 is
questions.e: 9 − 6 + 4 = 7. Adding the middle term instead of subtracting gives 9 + 6 + 4 = 19.

questions.s: The domain of the real function f(x) = √(x − 2)/(x − 5) is
questions.e: The square root needs x − 2 ≥ 0, so x ≥ 2, and the denominator needs x ≠ 5. Together: x ≥ 2 with x ≠ 5. 'x ≠ 5' alone forgets the square root condition.

questions.s: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. The largest angle is
questions.e: The angles add up to 180°, so one part is 180° ÷ 9 = 20° and the largest angle is 4 × 20° = 80°. 60° is the middle angle (3 parts).

questions.s: The supplement of an angle of 65° is
questions.e: Supplementary angles add up to 180°, so the supplement is 180° − 65° = 115°. 25° is the complement (adding to 90°).

questions.s: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are 6 cm and 8 cm. The hypotenuse is
questions.e: By Pythagoras, h² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, so h = 10 cm. 14 cm simply adds the two sides, and √28 subtracts the squares.

questions.s: A 13 m ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 5 m from the wall on level ground. The height at which it touches the wall is
questions.e: The ladder is the hypotenuse: height² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so the height is 12 m. √194 comes from adding the squares, which would make the ladder a leg instead of the hypotenuse.

questions.s: Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is
questions.e: The exterior angle is 360° ÷ 6 = 60°, so each interior angle is 180° − 60° = 120°. 60° is the exterior angle, and 108° belongs to a regular pentagon.

questions.s: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. The number of sides of the polygon is
questions.e: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°, so n = 360 ÷ 24 = 15. Using 180 instead of 360 would give 7.5, which is impossible.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, the area of a circle of radius 7 cm is
questions.e: Area = πr² = 22/7 × 49 = 154 cm². 44 cm is the circumference, and 616 cm² comes from using the diameter 14 cm as the radius.

questions.s: A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 70 cm. Taking π = 22/7, the number of complete turns it makes in covering 1.1 km is
questions.e: Circumference = πd = 22/7 × 70 = 220 cm = 2.2 m, and 1.1 km = 1,100 m, so the wheel turns 1,100 ÷ 2.2 = 500 times. Using 70 cm as the radius gives a 440 cm circumference and the wrong answer 250.

questions.s: A trapezium has parallel sides of 10 cm and 16 cm and a perpendicular distance of 6 cm between them. Its area is
questions.e: Area = ½(a + b)h = ½ × 26 × 6 = 78 cm². 156 cm² forgets the factor ½, and 96 cm² uses only the longer side (16 × 6).

questions.s: At the same time of day in Quetta, a vertical pole 3 m high casts a shadow 2 m long and a tower casts a shadow 30 m long. The height of the tower is
questions.e: The triangles formed are similar, so height/shadow is the same: h/30 = 3/2, giving h = 45 m. 20 m comes from inverting the ratio (30 × 2/3).

questions.s: A water tank in the shape of a cuboid measures 2 m by 1.5 m by 1 m. Its capacity is (1 m³ = 1,000 litres)
questions.e: Volume = 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 m³ = 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 litres. 3 litres forgets to convert cubic metres to litres.

questions.s: Taking π = 22/7, the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is
questions.e: V = πr²h = 22/7 × 49 × 10 = 154 × 10 = 1,540 cm³. 440 cm² is the curved surface area (2πrh), not the volume.

questions.s: The total surface area of a cube is 150 cm². Its volume is
questions.e: 6a² = 150 gives a² = 25 and a = 5 cm, so the volume is 5³ = 125 cm³. 25 is the area of one face, not the volume.

questions.s: The distance between the points (1, 2) and (4, 6) is
questions.e: d = √[(4 − 1)² + (6 − 2)²] = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. 7 adds the differences 3 + 4 without squaring, and 25 forgets the square root.

questions.s: The midpoint of the line segment joining (−2, 5) and (6, −1) is
questions.e: Midpoint = ((−2 + 6)/2, (5 − 1)/2) = (2, 2). (4, 4) is the sum of the coordinates without halving.

questions.s: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, then tan θ equals
questions.e: Take opposite = 3 and hypotenuse = 5; then adjacent = √(25 − 9) = 4, so tan θ = 3/4. 4/5 is cos θ and 4/3 is cot θ.

questions.s: The value of sin 30° + cos 60° is
questions.e: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so the sum is 1. Giving 1/2 counts only one of the two terms.

questions.s: From a point on level ground 30 m from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60°. The height of the tower is
questions.e: tan 60° = h/30, so h = 30 × √3 = 30√3 m. 10√3 m uses tan 30° = 1/√3 instead of tan 60°.

questions.s: From a point on level ground the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30°. After walking 20 m straight towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. The height of the tower is
questions.e: Let x be the final distance: h = x√3 and h = (x + 20)/√3. Equating, 3x = x + 20, so x = 10 and h = 10√3 m. 10 m is the remaining distance to the tower, not its height.

questions.s: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is any other point on the circle. The angle ACB is
questions.e: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so ∠ACB = 90°. 180° is the angle at the centre subtended by the diameter, which is twice the angle at the circumference.

questions.s: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of 80° at the centre. The angle it subtends at a point on the remaining part of the circle is
questions.e: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc, so the angle is 80° ÷ 2 = 40°. 160° doubles instead of halving.

questions.s: The diagonal of a rectangle is 25 cm and one of its sides is 7 cm. The area of the rectangle is
questions.e: The other side is √(25² − 7²) = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 cm, so the area is 24 × 7 = 168 cm². 175 cm² multiplies the diagonal by the side, and 84 cm² is the area of only one of the two triangles.

questions.s: The area of an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm is
questions.e: Area = (√3/4)a² = (√3/4) × 36 = 9√3 cm². 18√3 cm² forgets the ½ in ½ × base × height (the height is 3√3 cm).

questions.s: A square is drawn inside a circle of radius 5 cm so that all four corners of the square lie on the circle. The area of the square is
questions.e: The diagonal of the square is a diameter, 10 cm, and the area of a square is d²/2 = 100/2 = 50 cm² (side 5√2 cm). 100 cm² treats the diameter as the side of the square.

questions.s: A rectangular lawn 30 m by 20 m has a path 2 m wide running all round it on the outside. Paving the path costs Rs 50 per m². The total cost is
questions.e: The outer rectangle is 34 m × 24 m = 816 m², so the path is 816 − 600 = 216 m² and costs 216 × 50 = Rs 10,800. Rs 10,000 uses perimeter × width (100 × 2 = 200 m²), which leaves out the four corner squares.

questions.s: The slope of a line perpendicular to y = 2x + 1 is
questions.e: Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1, so m = −1/2. A slope of 2 gives a parallel line, and −2 only changes the sign without taking the reciprocal.

questions.s: The equation of the line with slope 3 passing through the point (1, 4) is
questions.e: y − 4 = 3(x − 1) gives y = 3x + 1; check: x = 1 gives y = 4. y = 3x + 4 wrongly uses the point's y-coordinate as the intercept.

questions.s: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one of the two opposite interior angles is 45°. The other opposite interior angle is
questions.e: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles, so the other angle is 110° − 45° = 65°. 70° is the adjacent interior angle (180° − 110°), not an opposite one.

questions.s: A cone has base radius 3 cm and vertical height 4 cm. Its curved surface area is
questions.e: Slant height l = √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm, so the curved surface area is πrl = π × 3 × 5 = 15π cm². 12π is the volume in cm³ (⅓πr²h), and 24π cm² adds the base to give the total surface area.

questions.s: If cos θ = 1/2 and θ is an acute angle, then θ equals
questions.e: cos 60° = 1/2, so θ = 60°. 30° is the angle whose sine is 1/2.

questions.s: For the matrix A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] (rows written inside the outer brackets), the element a₂₃ is
questions.e: a₂₃ is the element in row 2, column 3, which is 6. The value 3 is a₁₃, from reading the column first in the wrong row.
Add corresponding elements: [[2 + 1, 1 + 0], [3 − 2, 4 + 5]] = [[3, 1], [1, 9]]. [[3, 1], [5, 9]] treats −2 as +2, and [[2, 0], [−6, 20]] multiplies the elements instead of adding.

questions.s: If A = [[1, −2], [0, 4]], then 3A equals
questions.e: A scalar multiplies every element: 3A = [[3, −6], [0, 12]]. [[3, −2], [0, 4]] multiplies only the first element, and [[4, 1], [3, 7]] adds 3 to each element.

questions.s: The determinant of the matrix [[5, 3], [2, 4]] is
questions.e: For [[a, b], [c, d]], the determinant is ad − bc = 5 × 4 − 3 × 2 = 20 − 6 = 14. 26 adds the two products instead of subtracting, and −14 subtracts them in the wrong order.

questions.s: If A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[2, 0], [1, 3]], then the product AB is
questions.e: Row by column: first row (1·2 + 2·1, 1·0 + 2·3) = (4, 6), second row (3·2 + 4·1, 3·0 + 4·3) = (10, 12). [[2, 4], [10, 14]] is BA, since matrix multiplication is not commutative, and [[2, 0], [3, 12]] multiplies matching elements only.

questions.s: The matrix [[x, 4], [1, x]] is singular for
questions.e: A singular matrix has determinant zero: x² − 4 = 0, so x = 2 or x = −2. 'x = 2 only' misses the negative root of x² = 4.

questions.s: The inverse of the matrix [[3, 1], [5, 2]] is
questions.e: The determinant is 3 × 2 − 1 × 5 = 1. Swap the diagonal elements and change the signs of the others: A⁻¹ = (1/1)[[2, −1], [−5, 3]]. [[3, −1], [−5, 2]] changes signs but forgets to swap the diagonal elements 3 and 2.

questions.s: The transpose of the matrix [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] is
questions.e: The transpose turns rows into columns, so the 2 × 3 matrix becomes 3 × 2: [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]]. [[4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3]] only swaps the rows and keeps the order 2 × 3.

questions.s: The determinant of the matrix [[1, 2, 0], [3, −1, 4], [0, 2, 1]] is
questions.e: Expand along the first row: 1[(−1)(1) − 4·2] − 2[3·1 − 4·0] + 0 = 1(−9) − 2(3) = −15. Using + instead of − for the second term gives −9 + 6 = −3.

questions.s: The system 3x + 2y = 12 and x + y = 5 is written as AX = B and solved using X = A⁻¹B. The solution is
questions.e: A = [[3, 2], [1, 1]] has |A| = 1 and A⁻¹ = [[1, −2], [−1, 3]], so x = 12 − 10 = 2 and y = −12 + 15 = 3. x = 4, y = 0 satisfies only the first equation.

questions.s: If A = [[2, 1], [1, 1]] and I is the 2 × 2 identity matrix, then A² − 3A + I equals
questions.e: A² = [[5, 3], [3, 2]] and 3A = [[6, 3], [3, 3]], so A² − 3A = [[−1, 0], [0, −1]] = −I; adding I gives the zero matrix. Forgetting to add I at the end leads to −I, not I.

questions.s: A is a 2 × 2 matrix with |A| = 5. The value of |3A| is
questions.e: Multiplying a 2 × 2 matrix by 3 multiplies each of its two rows by 3, so |3A| = 3² × |A| = 9 × 5 = 45. 15 multiplies the determinant by 3 only once, and 135 uses 3³, which is the rule for a 3 × 3 matrix.

questions.s: For which value of k does the system kx + 2y = 5, 3x + 6y = 8 fail to have a unique solution?
questions.e: A unique solution needs the coefficient determinant to be non-zero: 6k − 2 × 3 = 6k − 6, which is zero when k = 1. k = 3 comes from comparing only the x-coefficients of the two equations.

questions.s: Sana buys 2 kg of sugar and 3 kg of flour, written as the row matrix Q = [2 3]. The prices are sugar Rs 150 per kg and flour Rs 200 per kg, written as the column matrix P = [[150], [200]]. The product QP gives her total bill as
questions.e: QP = 2 × 150 + 3 × 200 = 300 + 600 = Rs 900. Rs 850 pairs each quantity with the wrong price (2 × 200 + 3 × 150).

questions.s: A square matrix whose determinant is zero is called
questions.e: A square matrix with determinant 0 is singular and has no inverse. A non-singular matrix is one whose determinant is not zero.

questions.s: The mean of 4, 7, 9, 10 and 15 is
questions.e: Mean = (4 + 7 + 9 + 10 + 15)/5 = 45/5 = 9. 45 is the total, which still has to be divided by the number of values.

questions.s: The median of 3, 8, 5, 12, 7 and 10 is
questions.e: In order the values are 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12; with six values the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th, (7 + 8)/2 = 7.5. 8.5 averages the two middle values of the unsorted list (5 and 12), which is wrong because the data must be ordered first.

questions.s: The mode of the data 2, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7 is
questions.e: The mode is the most frequent value: 6 occurs three times, more than any other. 3 is how often the mode occurs, not the mode itself.

questions.s: The range of the data 12, 25, 7, 18, 30 is
questions.e: Range = largest − smallest = 30 − 7 = 23. 18 subtracts the first value from the second-largest, and 37 adds the extremes instead of subtracting.

questions.s: The standard deviation of the data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (taking the population standard deviation) is
questions.e: The mean is 6 and the squared deviations are 16, 4, 0, 4, 16, totalling 40. Variance = 40/5 = 8, so SD = √8 = 2√2. 8 is the variance, which still needs a square root.

questions.s: A data set has mean 20 and standard deviation 4. If 5 is added to every value, the new mean and new standard deviation are
questions.e: Adding a constant shifts every value, so the mean becomes 20 + 5 = 25, but the spread is unchanged and the SD stays 4. Adding 5 to the SD as well (giving 9) is the usual mistake.

questions.s: In an Islamabad college, section A has 30 students with a mean score of 60 and section B has 20 students with a mean score of 70. The mean score of all 50 students is
questions.e: Combined mean = (30 × 60 + 20 × 70)/50 = (1,800 + 1,400)/50 = 3,200/50 = 64. 65 is the simple average of the two means, which ignores that section A is larger.

questions.s: The table shows the marks scored by 10 students in a quiz. The mean mark is
questions.e: Mean = Σfx/Σf = (20 + 60 + 120 + 40)/10 = 240/10 = 24. 25 is the average of the four mark values, which ignores how many students got each mark.

questions.s: Ali has 4 shirts and 3 pairs of trousers. The number of different shirt-and-trousers outfits he can wear is
questions.e: By the multiplication principle, 4 × 3 = 12 outfits. Adding (4 + 3 = 7) counts the items, not the pairings.

questions.s: In how many ways can 5 students stand in a row for a photograph?
questions.e: The number of arrangements is 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. 720 is 6!, and 25 is 5², which allows the same student in more than one place.

questions.s: How many three-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 if no digit is repeated?
questions.e: There are 6 choices for the first digit, 5 for the second and 4 for the third: 6 × 5 × 4 = ⁶P₃ = 120. 216 = 6³ allows repetition, and 20 = ⁶C₃ ignores the order of the digits.

questions.s: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 8 people?
questions.e: Order does not matter, so the number is ⁸C₃ = (8 × 7 × 6)/(3 × 2 × 1) = 56. 336 = ⁸P₃ counts ordered selections, as if the members held different posts.

questions.s: The number of different arrangements of all the letters of the word PAKISTAN is
questions.e: PAKISTAN has 8 letters with A occurring twice, so the number is 8!/2! = 40,320/2 = 20,160. 40,320 treats the two A's as different letters.

questions.s: A team of 2 men and 2 women is to be chosen from 5 men and 4 women. The number of possible teams is
questions.e: Men can be chosen in ⁵C₂ = 10 ways and women in ⁴C₂ = 6 ways, so there are 10 × 6 = 60 teams. 126 = ⁹C₄ ignores the 2-and-2 condition, and 16 adds the two counts instead of multiplying.

questions.s: A fair six-sided die is thrown once. The probability that it shows a prime number is
questions.e: The primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2. 1/3 forgets that 2 is prime, and 1 is not a prime number.

questions.s: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green marbles. One marble is taken at random. The probability that it is blue is
questions.e: There are 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 marbles and 3 are blue, so P(blue) = 3/10. 3/7 compares blue with non-blue marbles (odds), not with the total.

questions.s: Three fair coins are tossed together. The probability of getting at least one head is
questions.e: There are 2³ = 8 equally likely outcomes and only TTT has no head, so P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8. 1/8 is the probability of no head at all, the complement of the event asked for.

questions.s: Two fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 8 is
questions.e: Of the 36 equally likely outcomes, (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3), (6, 2) give 8, so P = 5/36. 1/11 treats the 11 possible sums 2 to 12 as equally likely, which they are not.

questions.s: A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. The probability that A and B occur together is
questions.e: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. 0.7 is P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.5 − 0.2, and 0.9 simply adds the probabilities.

questions.s: The probability that it will rain in Lahore tomorrow is 0.35. The probability that it will not rain is
questions.e: P(not A) = 1 − P(A) = 1 − 0.35 = 0.65. 0.5 assumes rain and no rain are equally likely.

questions.s: A box contains 4 red and 6 white balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other without replacement. The probability that both are red is
questions.e: P = 4/10 × 3/9 = 12/90 = 2/15, since after one red ball is removed only 3 red balls remain among 9. 4/25 = (4/10)² is the answer with replacement.

questions.s: One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. The probability that it is a king or a heart is
questions.e: P(king or heart) = 4/52 + 13/52 − 1/52 = 16/52 = 4/13; the king of hearts is subtracted once because it was counted twice. 17/52 forgets this overlap.

questions.s: The mean of six numbers is 15. When one number is removed, the mean of the remaining five is 14. The number removed is
questions.e: The total falls from 6 × 15 = 90 to 5 × 14 = 70, so the removed number is 90 − 70 = 20. Answering 1 uses only the change in the mean (15 − 14), not the change in the total.

questions.s: The table shows the monthly sales of a shop in Karachi. The percentage increase in sales from March to April is
questions.e: Increase = 75 − 60 = 15 thousand, and 15/60 × 100 = 25%. 20% divides the increase by the April figure (15/75) instead of the earlier March figure.

questions.s: The table shows the number of children in 20 families. The median number of children is
questions.e: With 20 families the median is the average of the 10th and 11th values. Cumulative frequencies are 3, 10, 14, …, so the 10th value is 2 and the 11th is 3, giving a median of 2.5. 2 is the mode, the most common value.

questions.s: The standard deviation of a set of values x is 3. The standard deviation of the values 2x + 5 is
questions.e: Multiplying every value by 2 doubles the spread, while adding 5 does not change it, so the new SD is 2 × 3 = 6. 11 wrongly applies the +5 to the standard deviation, and 36 is the new variance.

questions.s: A student must answer 4 of the 7 questions on a paper, and question 1 is compulsory. The number of ways she can choose her questions is
questions.e: Question 1 is fixed, so she chooses the other 3 from the remaining 6: ⁶C₃ = 20. 35 = ⁷C₄ ignores the compulsory question.

questions.s: A fair die is thrown twice. The probability of getting at least one six is
questions.e: P(no six in two throws) = 5/6 × 5/6 = 25/36, so P(at least one six) = 1 − 25/36 = 11/36. 1/3 adds 1/6 + 1/6 and counts the double six twice; 5/18 = 10/36 is the chance of exactly one six.

questions.s: In how many ways can 6 friends be seated around a circular table, if only their positions relative to each other matter?
questions.e: For a circular arrangement fix one person and arrange the rest: (6 − 1)! = 5! = 120. 720 = 6! counts the rotations of the same seating as different.

questions.s: A family in Multan spends Rs 60,000 a month. In a pie chart of its spending, the sector for rent has an angle of 90°. The monthly rent is
questions.e: The rent's share is 90°/360° = 1/4, so the rent is 60,000 ÷ 4 = Rs 15,000. Rs 54,000 treats the 90 degrees as 90 per cent.

questions.s: The value of lim (x → 2) of (3x + 1) is
questions.e: A polynomial is continuous, so substitute x = 2: 3(2) + 1 = 7. Giving 6 drops the constant term 1.

questions.s: The value of lim (x → 3) of (x² − 9)/(x − 3) is
questions.e: Direct substitution gives 0/0, so factorise: (x − 3)(x + 3)/(x − 3) = x + 3 for x ≠ 3, and the limit is 3 + 3 = 6. 'Undefined' confuses the value of the function at x = 3 with its limit.

questions.s: The value of lim (x → ∞) of (3x² + 2)/(x² − 5) is
questions.e: Divide top and bottom by x²: (3 + 2/x²)/(1 − 5/x²) → 3/1 = 3 as x → ∞. −2/5 is the value at x = 0, not the limit at infinity.

questions.s: The derivative of x⁴ with respect to x is
questions.e: By the power rule d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹, so d/dx(x⁴) = 4x³. x⁵/5 is the integral of x⁴, not its derivative.

questions.s: If f(x) = 5x³ − 2x² + 7x − 1, then f′(x) equals
questions.e: Differentiate term by term: 15x² − 4x + 7, and the constant −1 has derivative 0. 15x² − 4x − 1 keeps the constant, which should vanish.

questions.s: The slope of the tangent to the curve y = x² − 3x + 2 at x = 4 is
questions.e: dy/dx = 2x − 3, which at x = 4 is 8 − 3 = 5. 6 is the y-value of the curve at x = 4, not the slope.

questions.s: A factory's cost of producing x units is C(x) = 2x² + 10x + 500 rupees. The marginal cost C′(x) when x = 20 is
questions.e: C′(x) = 4x + 10, so C′(20) = 80 + 10 = Rs 90 per unit. Rs 1,500 is the total cost C(20), and Rs 50 differentiates 2x² as 2x.

questions.s: The area of a square of side s is A = s². The rate of change of A with respect to s when s = 5 is
questions.e: dA/ds = 2s, which is 2 × 5 = 10 when s = 5. 25 is the area itself, not its rate of change.

questions.s: A firm's profit is P(x) = −x² + 40x − 100 thousand rupees when it sells x hundred units. Its maximum profit is
questions.e: P′(x) = −2x + 40 = 0 gives x = 20, and P″ = −2 < 0 confirms a maximum. P(20) = −400 + 800 − 100 = 300, i.e. Rs 300 thousand. 20 is the number of hundreds of units at the maximum, not the profit.

questions.s: A shopkeeper finds that he can sell x units of a product per day at a price of (100 − 2x) rupees each. His maximum possible daily revenue is
questions.e: Revenue R = x(100 − 2x) = 100x − 2x², so R′ = 100 − 4x = 0 at x = 25. R(25) = 2,500 − 1,250 = Rs 1,250. Rs 2,500 is only the 100x part at x = 25 and ignores the falling price.

questions.s: ∫ 3x² dx equals
questions.e: ∫ xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C, so ∫ 3x² dx = 3 × x³/3 + C = x³ + C. 6x + C is the derivative of 3x², not its integral.

questions.s: ∫ (4x³ − 6x + 2) dx equals
questions.e: Integrate term by term: 4x⁴/4 − 6x²/2 + 2x + C = x⁴ − 3x² + 2x + C. 12x² − 6 differentiates instead of integrating, and x⁴ − 6x² forgets to divide −6x² by 2.

questions.s: The value of the definite integral of (3x² + 1) from x = 0 to x = 2 is
questions.e: An antiderivative is x³ + x, so the integral is (8 + 2) − 0 = 10. 8 forgets to integrate the constant 1.

questions.s: The area between the curve y = x², the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 3 is
questions.e: Area = ∫₀³ x² dx = [x³/3]₀³ = 27/3 = 9 square units. 27 forgets to divide by 3, and 6 is the slope dy/dx = 2x at x = 3.

questions.s: The derivative of the constant function f(x) = 7 is
questions.e: A constant does not change as x changes, so its derivative is 0. 7x is the integral of 7, not its derivative.

questions.s: The total cost of making x items is C(x) = x² + 400 rupees, so the average cost per item is x + 400/x. The minimum average cost per item is
questions.e: d/dx(x + 400/x) = 1 − 400/x² = 0 gives x = 20, and the average cost there is 20 + 400/20 = 20 + 20 = Rs 40. Rs 20 is the number of items, not the cost.

questions.s: The local maximum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x is
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 at x = ±1, and f″(x) = 6x is negative at x = −1, so the maximum is at x = −1: f(−1) = −1 + 3 = 2. −2 is the local minimum value at x = 1.

questions.s: The tangent to the curve y = x² − 8x + 3 is horizontal at x equal to
questions.e: A horizontal tangent has slope 0: dy/dx = 2x − 8 = 0 gives x = 4. −4 comes from a sign error in solving 2x − 8 = 0.

questions.s: A company's revenue t years after starting is R(t) = 5t² + 20t lakh rupees. The rate at which its revenue is growing at t = 3 is (in lakh rupees per year)
questions.e: R′(t) = 10t + 20, so R′(3) = 30 + 20 = 50 lakh rupees per year. 105 is the revenue R(3) itself, not its rate of change.

questions.s: The value of lim (x → 0) of (x² + 5x)/x is
questions.e: For x ≠ 0, (x² + 5x)/x = x + 5, so the limit as x → 0 is 5. Answering 0 substitutes x = 0 in the numerator only and ignores the 0 in the denominator.
